resources.title: Bas's CMLL cheat sheet (ALGS-CMLL.jpg)
resources.author: Basilio Noris (b4silio), basilio.dev/cubing
resources.level: beginner-intermediate (learning full CMLL; the EO box suits beginners)
resources.summary: A single JPEG (1118x502 px, 285 KB) from the 'Bas's guides and algsheets' section of basilio.dev/cubing. It fits all 42 CMLL cases on one landscape image, in 8 boxes by corner-orientation group: Sune 6, Anti-Sune 6, Pi 6, H 4, O 2, U 6, T 6, L 6. Each case has a tiny U-face icon with arrows marking the side-sticker pattern, then a pattern name, then the alg with its pre-AUF in parentheses, then a one-line mnemonic built from trigger names ('Hedge [U2R]', 'Sledge rUr', 'F triple rev-sexy F', 'Antisune Backantisune'). Pattern names: Left Bar, Right Bar, Columns, Up Slash, Down Slash and X for S/AS/Pi. H uses Column, Rows, Right Bar and Row; O uses Diag and Adj. U and T add Upper Row, Bottom Row and Rows. L uses Bar V, Bar + Row, Row Climbing, Slanted F, Diag N and Diag X. About 12 algs carry a small OLL-shape icon. It marks algs that are also standard 3x3 OLL algs ('Std Fish', 'Std Turtle', 'Std Headlights', 'Std Tie'), which helps CFOP converts. A bottom-left box shows 9 LSE edge-orientation (4a) states as 3D cubes, with misoriented stickers in purple and an M/U solution under each. One of them is a 6-flip alg (R U' r' U' M' U r U r'). I transcribed every alg into the saved text file. The parent page links further sheets, including ALGS-EOLR.jpg (Roux LSE), which this batch does not cover.

resources.title: CMLL Visualiser
resources.author: Hubert Badocha (GitHub: badochov)
resources.summary: A static jQuery tool from the repo github.com/badochov/cmll-visualiser: 11 commits from 2020-02-11 to 2022-06-22, about 900 lines of JS. You paste CMLL algs, one per line, and press Generate (or Enter). For each alg it draws a 2D diagram of the side effect on the 6 LSE edges: the four U corners with their side stickers (CLL), the UB/UL/UR/UF edges, and DB and DF as squares above and below. Flipped edges are filled (light blue by default), and red arrows show where each edge goes (EP). If the alg breaks the first two blocks, it draws a big red X. That check is coarse: it only flags block edges that are both moved and flipped, and D corners that are both moved and twisted. Navigation is by prev/next buttons or the arrow keys, with an 'n/N' counter and the alg shown above. Syntax is SiGN, with wide moves in lower case. A post-CMLL AUF is written as a bracketed premove ('[U]') at the start. Text after '//' is a comment, shown only in the PDF. The settings drawer (tune icon) has EO, EP and CLL layer toggles, Spectrum colour pickers (top, left, right, front and back faces, flipped edge, arrows, outline, background), 'Restore default colors' and a PDF file name. The Download button (or the Insert key) builds an A4 PDF with jsPDF: 6 diagrams per page in two columns, alg in bold and comment underneath. Right-click saves a single PNG. I drove it with 7 algs; the screenshots are saved. It is the only resource in this batch that shows how a CMLL alg changes the LSE state, which matters for EO prediction and for choosing between alg variants.

Do not copy the code; the idea is easy to reimplement on the app's own cube model. The session's GitHub policy refused GitHub API metadata for this repo, but a read-only git clone of the public repo worked.

resources.author: Iuri (surname not shown; Drive owner hidden)
resources.summary: A public Google Drive folder; no sign-in needed. It has 8 subfolders by orientation group (Antisune, H, L, O, Pi, Sune, T, U), created 30 Dec 2018. Together they hold 41 MP4 execution videos (about 1.76 GB, uploaded Feb to Aug 2019). There is also a Google Sheet, 'Iuri's OH CMLLs', modified 7 Jun 2020. Videos per folder: Antisune 6, H 4, L 6, O 1 (only 'O3 (Adj)'), Pi 6 (Pi1-4 and Pi6, plus an alternative Pi3), Sune 7 (S1-S6 plus an unnamed clip), T 6, U 5 (no U2). File names give the case number and pattern nicknames, e.g. 'aS1 (Right Bar/Pure)', 'S5 (X Checkerboard/L Apple)', 'L2 (Back Comm)', 'T3 (L Sexy sledge)', 'Pi3 (X/Checkerboard) - alt'. The three thumbnails I fetched show a real cube filmed close up and held in the left hand. The sheet lists one OH alg for each of 42 cases in the same numbering: O3 and O6; H1, H2, H3, H6; Pi1-6; U1-6; T1-6; S1-6; As1-6; L1-6. Its case-image cells are broken (#REF!). The algs use R/U/F/r moves, D-move headlights (R2 D R' U2 R D' R' U2 R') and an occasional rotation (H2: R' U' R U' R' U' z U z' U' R U L'). The sheet links back to the parent 'Iuri's CMLLs' folder as 'Executions'.

resources.title: CMLL Prediction (athefre's site)
resources.author: Michael James Straughan (Athefre)
resources.summary: A Google Sites page (techniques developed from July 2022) on predicting CMLL during the second-block last pair, to remove the CMLL recognition pause. It compares 7 recognition systems by what you look at. Straughan, by object: find the F and R stickers. Straughan, by position: find the U-layer stickers among UFL, UFR and UBR, then check a pattern. ATCRM: orientation of the L/R or F/B stickers, then 2 fixed stickers. NMCMLL: the same first step, then 4 fixed stickers. Original NMCMLL: L/R or F/B orientation, then U-sticker orientation. U sticker + pattern: the usual method. Hyperorientations: U orientation, then F/B or L/R orientation. Sticker counts are Straughan 4, ATCRM 5, and 6 each for U sticker + pattern and Hyperorientations. Liam Highducheck points out that Straughan is really 3 tracked stickers, since one corner carries two of them. Sections: Straughan (4 patterns per alg, many of them mirrors); ATCRM (credits Zhouheng Sun with the idea that recognising non-U stickers first, as in NMCMLL, suits prediction); OCLL prediction; 'Intuitive CP'; overall thoughts. OCLL prediction links a sheet, 'View Orientation Cases', with tabs dFR and dBR. For each last-pair insert it names the 3 target corners, how they move and which to check first, plus a 3x9 grid mapping the 27 twist states of those corners to the resulting OCLL shape (O, S, AS, H, Pi, T, U, L). The inserts are r U' r' / R U' R', r U r' / R U R', R U2 R', U r' U' r / U R' U' R, and r' U r / R' U R. Intuitive CP is his own method from 2006: during the last pair, find three L/R (or F/B) stickers, check two opposite-coloured ones and the relative position of their U stickers (+ or -), then find one more U sticker. Diagonal L/R stickers always mean an adjacent swap. The named outcomes are Correct, Opposite Swap, Swap Left, Swap Right, and Front/Left/Back/Right Swap. Faster variants check F/B stickers instead of U stickers, with the rules inverted. The text mentions 'orientation sticker targeting', but that section is not on the live page.

resources.title: Multi angle CxLL recog (Drive folder of 5 Google Docs)
resources.author: Not named (Drive owner hidden); Anti-Sune images credited to Zhouheng Sun
resources.level: intermediate-advanced (beginners: learn one angle; advanced: learn both)
resources.summary: A public Drive folder named 'Multi angle CxLL recog' with 5 Google Docs dated Jun 2020 to May 2021: Anti-Sune (a shortcut), L, O, Sune, and 'T (and U)'. There are no H or Pi docs; the T doc says its system works the same way for U. The goal is to recognise every case from whatever angle it appears, using only the R, U and F faces, without an extra AUF or peeking at L. The docs say the systems also work for CLL, EG and COLL. They list one RH CMLL alg per case only to identify it and link Anto's 2H CMLL list for algs. Each doc uses 3D cube images with only the recognition stickers coloured and arrows between them: white = same colour, pink/purple = opposite colours, grey = adjacent colours, black = swapped corners (O doc). Sune and Anti-Sune have two systems: angle 1 (4 stickers, like the usual U/T/H/Pi method) and angle 2 (3 stickers, two comparisons). L also has two: angle 1 compares the two U-face stickers (same, adjacent or opposite narrows it to 2 cases, then one extra sticker decides; for pure/diag, count whether you see 4 colours or 2), and angle 2 is U2 away, with recognitions swapped within each row. T/U uses one system from any angle, based on which oriented corner carries both U-sticker colours. O counts adjacent corner pairs solved relative to each other. Two pairs means solved; one pair means an adjacent swap of the other two. With no pairs, look for opposite colours on one face: if only one face shows them, those two corners are an adjacent swap; if both F and R do, it is a diagonal swap. I saved the text exports and the HTML exports with images.

resources.title: OLLCP - SpeedCubeDB
resources.author: SpeedCubeDB, created by Gil Zussman (algs crowd-submitted and voted)
resources.summary: An index page for OLLCP (orientation of the last layer plus corner permutation, leaving only EPLL), with a two-line description noting that COLL is a subset. It links 57 subpages, one per OLL number, and I rendered all of them. Each lists 6 corner-permutation cases, for 342 entries in total; symmetric OLLs still list 6, so some entries are duplicates. OLLCP21-27 are the edges-oriented (COLL) part. Each case shows a setup alg, the top 3-5 community algs (with rotations and wide moves) and a 'More Algorithms' expander. The page chrome is the same as SBLS on this site: cross-colour selector, Related Sets, learnt/learning flags, votes, animated player, ads and a donate link. SCDB's own trainer (/t) covers only PLL. This is a generic last-layer set, not a Roux one. rouxcubing.com lists it under CMLL > Pinkie Pie, next to Kian's explainer video and Sevilz's OLLCP sheet. Pinkie Pie is an advanced trick that uses an OLLCP alg at the CMLL step so U edges are oriented too. I did not watch the video, so its exact trigger condition is unverified. roux-trainers already has an unfinished OLLCP trainer: ollcp_algs_raw in src/lib/Algs.tsx, with groups 13, 14, 34, 39, 45, 51 and 56, and OllcpTrainerView commented out in AppView.tsx ('TODO: build this').

resources.title: NMCMLL (athefre's site)
resources.author: Michael James Straughan (Athefre); no byline on the page itself
resources.summary: A short Google Sites page titled 'NMCMLL', at the URL /roux/roux. NMCMLL is CMLL for non-matching blocks, where the two blocks have different D colours, so the U corners do not share one U colour. Cases are therefore defined and recognised by the L/R-colour stickers. Recognition rule: first check the orientation of the L/R stickers (drawn as white and yellow), then look for matching stickers at the spots marked by red lines. The page has one large chart: 23 orientation icons with red marker lines, each followed by the case patterns that share it, labelled like 'E1-2', 'H2/H4-1' or 'A6' (case, plus pattern 1 or 2). Below it, 8 embedded tables (groups A-H) give Case, AUF 1, AUF 2 and Alg: A1 (solved), A2, A6; B1-B6 through G1-G6; H1, H2/H4, H3/H5, H6. That is 42 algs plus solved, using R, L, U, F, B and D moves (e.g. B2: R' U' R U' R' U R' D' R U R' D R2). The two AUF columns are probably the AUFs for patterns -1 and -2. The page says an upgraded recognition called 'ACRM' exists; the CMLL prediction page calls it ATCRM. roux-trainers already has this L/R-first idea as 'NMCLL Recog Mode' (L/R or F/B), with the same 23 groups mapped to regular CMLL cases (nmcll_to_cmll_mapping and nmcll_display_parity in src/lib/Algs.tsx). The speedsolving.com wiki page on NMCMLL returned 403 from the proxy, so I did not use it.

resources.title: ACMLL (athefre's site)
resources.author: Michael James Straughan (Athefre); 2-look docs by junnoske
resources.summary: A Google Sites page. ACMLL is a family of alg sets that solve CMLL when F2B is deliberately left imperfect (a pair misoriented, swapped or placed outside its block), fixing the blocks during CMLL. Listed benefits: 2-6 moves saved on SB (more if also used in FB), deeper inspection and a step towards non-linear F2B, and better ergonomics, since pairs go in with U and R only, without r U r' flips or slices. On recognition: Straughan patterns are identical to CMLL's. With U-sticker recognition there are only three orientation types (CLL, TCLL+ and TCLL-), so only TCLL+ and TCLL- are new. You know which defect you built, so you never check the blocks. Sets, each with a Straughan-recognition sheet and a U-sticker sheet: Flipped Pair (FR 9.81 moves / 11.81 MCC, BR 9.67 / 12.35, against normal CMLL 10.02 / 12.31 from the Roux Discord 2H sheet); Outside (DFr 9.63 / 13.11, DBr 10.05 / 12.47); Swapped Pairs; Front Cycle; Spiral (two adjacent pairs swapped in one block). junnoske made 2-look docs for Flipped Pair and Spiral: look 1 fixes F2B and corner orientation (sorted by the number of oriented corners), look 2 solves CP (adjacent or diagonal). Recommended order: Flipped Pair FR and BR, Outside, Swap FL/FR, Front Cycle. Guiding rule: insert the last pair keeping its current orientation, and do not move the 1x2x2 until the pair's final move. The page asks for help generating more sets and suggests a batch solver to rank them by movecount. Its 'Credit / To do' heading is empty. I downloaded all 12 linked sheets. Each Straughan tab has 162 recognition codes. The U-sticker sheets group about 43 cases per set into A-H (A 6, B 6, C 4, D 6, E 6, F 6, G 6, H 3). The sheets also hold template, AUF-table, 'OH Codes' and batch-solver tabs.
